role: Crash-safety net for raw RR beats: writes every recording's beats to RRBackup/ in the App Group container (one-shot encrypted single-file JSON, or append-only header+JSONL via RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift), keeps a JSON index of backups, and serves retrieve/list/discard/purge/reconcile APIs to recovery, archive and diagnostics code.
types: RawRRBackup: class (@unchecked Sendable) — raw RR backup store; extended by an in-file extension (holdsBackup, writeOneShot), RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift, RawRRBackup+IndexRecovery.swift and SessionStorageDiagnostic.swift
RawRRBackup.BackupEntry: struct (Codable) — decoded backup (id, captureDate, deviceId, points, hash)
RawRRBackup.BackupHeader: struct (Codable) — header file of the append-only format
RawRRBackup.BackupIndex: struct (Codable) — index row (fileName for one-shot, backedUpCount for append-only, archived flag, lastBackupTime) with schemaVersion key
RawRRBackup.TerminationForensicsSummary: struct — static lockless view of one index row for CrashLogManager
state: file:{AppGroup group.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery or Documents or tmp}/RRBackup/ (AppConfig.backupDirectoryName)
file:RRBackup/<uuid>_<stamp>.json (one-shot backup, stamp = write time in ms raised past any taken name; older files carry whole seconds; encrypted when EncryptionManager available)
file:RRBackup/<uuid>_header.json, file:RRBackup/<uuid>_points.jsonl (append-only format; point lines sealed by EncryptionManager when the key is reachable)
toplevel: Stored-property initializers: index = [], indexReadFailed = false, fileManager = FileManager.default, indexLock = NSLock(), appendQueue serial utility queue, lineEncoder closure (82). BackupIndex declares CodingKeys including schemaVersion. The class is @unchecked Sendable relying on indexLock + appendQueue; only incrementalBackup and resetInMemoryStateAfterPurge/reencryptPendingBackups run on appendQueue — backup(), markAsArchived, discardBackup, reconcile*, purge mutate index under indexLock only.

One-shot backup: refuses empty points; via replaceableIndexEntry merges an index the launch could not read (throws while unreadable) and refuses to replace an existing backup with more beats; builds the entry (captureDate = caller's, else the existing row's, else now; integrityHash); writeOneShot writes it under a never-reused <uuid>_<ms>.json name and replaces and saves the index row (on a failed save the previous row is restored and the new file removed); only then deletes the session's append-only files and the previous one-shot file (removeReplacedFile; the names always differ now). Returns the entry.

branches.cond: index unreadable, or existing row holds more beats than points.count

Encodes the entry (encrypted when possible). Plaintext is recorded in the raw-backup PendingEncryptionLedger before its write; the bytes are written atomically with .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication when encrypted, .completeFileProtection when plaintext. A write that throws puts the ledger back as it was (an id that was not pending is cleared; one that was stays queued, so a failed re-encryption keeps its retry) and rethrows. An encrypted write clears the entry only after it lands. Internal (not private) so tests can drive a failing write.

branches.effect: true: until-first-auth protection; false: complete protection

Names the one-shot file with OneShotBackupName.make (write time in ms, raised past any name that is the existing row's file or already on disk), writes the entry there (writeEntry: encrypted, or plaintext + re-encryption ledger), then reindexes the session to that file. If reindex's index save throws (reindex has already restored the previous row in memory), removes the new, unindexed file and rethrows, so the restored row still names its own intact file with its own hash. Returns the file name.

flags.text: When reindex's save throws, writeEntry has already updated the raw-backup PendingEncryptionLedger for the NEW file (cleared if it was encrypted); if the still-indexed old one-shot file was plaintext, it then drops off the re-encryption queue while staying on disk unencrypted.
